text:
alice_ml: Heads-up, q8 bring-up for orpheus-7b-long (64k) showing a reproducible token-echo/divergence around ~32k tokens when the priming anchor crosses a chunk boundary. Uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-dev/triage/1768882001/artifacts.tar.gz :eyes:

alice_ml: Quick repro command I used:
```
python repro.py --model orpheus-7b-long-q8 --ctx 65536 --prompt tests/long_anchor.txt --seed 42 --max-tokens 40000 --no-cache-sharding --stream
```

alice_ml: Minimal log snippet (truncated):
```
[2026-03-22T18:20:11Z] token_idx=32760 token="the"
[2026-03-22T18:20:11Z] token_idx=32761 token="the"
[2026-03-22T18:20:11Z] token_idx=32762 token="the"
[2026-03-22T18:20:12Z] perplexity jump from 12.3 -> 198.7
```

ben_infra: interesting. could be RoPE phase wrap interacting with quantized KV indices or a misapplied rotary scale. did you run with the same kernel build as baseline?

alice_ml: yes same binary, but this build used q8 kernel variant. baseline float32 on same infra doesn't show echo. int4 experiment also showed softer symptoms but not full-on repetition.

carla_research: two hypotheses: 1) rotary phase scaling wasn't re-applied after quantization step and we have an off-by-stride when serializing KV shards, 2) priming crosses the shard boundary and offset normalization differs under q8 math.

carla_research: can you dump KV keys around the boundary? compare key norms pre/post quantization. sample script:
```python
# dump keys at boundary
for shard in shards_around(32768):
    print(shard.id, shard.start, shard.end, norm(shard.kv_keys))
```

alice_ml: I uploaded key_dumps/ in the artifact tar. norms look ~same but there are small bit-level differences (expected). i can run an exact byte-compare of serialized shards.

dave_ops: also note: we rolled a runtime kernel patch yesterday (sched v2) that touched NVTX / stream ordering. Kernel version: rwinfer-1.9.3-q8. If serialization ordering slipped, prefill could interleave keys incorrectly. cc @ben_infra

ben_infra: good catch. I'll check the CI staging rollout history vs your timestamps. if the kernel changed async memcpy ordering it could reorder prefill fragments.

elaine_eval: from eval side, this shows up as severe long-context quality regression on our longform summarization benchmark. BLEU-like continuity drops and hallucination increases once anchor crosses 30k. we need a deterministic repro for A/B.

alice_ml: making a pared-down deterministic repro now. one more wrinkle: reproduces only when `--no-cache-sharding` flag set to false (i.e., when sharding is enabled). with sharding disabled it's fine. that points to shard alignment bug.

carla_research: ok that narrows it. please run a tiny experiment: generate tokens with `--ctx=65536` but with a synthetic prompt that repeats a known pattern crossing the boundary. look for phase drift in attention scores. snippet to dump attn diag:
```python
attn_diag = model.inspect_attn(layer=10, head=3, token_idx=range(32750,32790))
np.savetxt('attn_diag.csv', attn_diag, delimiter=',')
```

alice_ml: running now, will attach attn_diag.csv. ETA ~5m.

kv-test-bot: Scheduled: longctx-shard-consistency x100 (priority=high) — queued on ded-gpu-pool-3, expected complete in ~30m.

ben_infra: I'm going to spin up a canary with the pre-patch kernel and same q8 model to see if condition disappears. if so, we have an ordering bug introduced by kernel.

dave_ops: FYI found one suspicious log from the rollout controller: `prefill_fragment_sequence: [0,1,3,2]` (should be 0,1,2,3). that's consistent with a reordering.

carla_research: if fragments can be delivered out-of-order, rotary pos embedding may be applied with wrong absolute indices -> phase mismatch. small quantization jitter would amplify.

elaine_eval: for triage, can we capture: 1) baseline float32 run, 2) q8 with pre-patch kernel, 3) q8 with post-patch kernel, each with same seed and prompt, and collect: token-level divergence index, BLEU continuity, attn_diag, kv_key_dumps? i'll run automated comparison once artifacts land.

alice_ml: ack. starting 3-run matrix now. uploading outputs to same s3 path with subdirs /baseline_fp32 /q8_prepatch /q8_postpatch.

ben_infra: i'll revert the rollout on ded-gpu-pool-3 to pre-patch for a canary if we see the triage reproduces on post-patch only.

carla_research: quick hack to detect mis-ordered fragments in future: compute monotonic checksums of prefill fragment indices during serialization and assert order at deserial. small patch I can submit as hotfix.

alice_ml: thanks. leaving the thread open while runs finish. attaching initial artefacts summary in the s3 bucket README inside the tar. will ping when comparisons done. :thumbsup:

kv-test-bot: longctx-shard-consistency run started (id=run-1768882001-1). I'll post results here when finished.
